slides.texte_overlay:
How to get genuinely cultured
in your 20s
Go to one cultural event a month. A concert, an exhibition, a play, a talk. Twelve new experiences a year give you more to talk about than any series.
Learn the story behind the things you love. Your favourite band's influences, your football club's history, your city's origins. Curiosity starts close to home.
Travel slowly when you can. Spend three days in one city instead of three cities in three days. You learn a place by walking and talking to locals.
Listen to a full album you've never heard, start to finish. Jazz, classical, a band from another country. Your taste grows when you step outside it.
Make learning a daily ritual. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and over a year that becomes a real, wide general culture.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Over a year that becomes a real, wide general culture.

slides.texte_overlay: Ask older people about their lives. Grandparents, neighbours, older colleagues. Their stories are living history you'll never find in a book.
Cook dishes from other countries. Every recipe has a story, a region and a tradition behind it. Culture is easier to remember when you can taste it.
